result.label: good
evidence: IPv4 octet uses `(?:25[0-5]|2[0-4][0-9]|1[0-9]{2}|[1-9]?[0-9])` correctly rejecting leading zeros and >255
Date pattern validates month 01-12 and day 01-31 with `(?:0[1-9]|1[0-2])` and `(?:0[1-9]|[12][0-9]|3[01])`, allowing Feb up to 29
Uses `\b`, `(?![\w-])`, and negative lookahead `(?!.*\b\d{4}-...)` to match only the last date and avoid alphanumeric-adjacent false matches
Only creates /app/regex.txt, no unrelated file edits or config changes
result.reason: The regex generalizes well beyond the visible test: correct octet ranges, proper date range constraints, word-boundary/lookahead guards against false matches, and last-date-in-line via negative lookahead. Minor concerns: the day pattern permits e.g. 04-31 (invalid calendar dates) but the task explicitly relaxes day/month validation. The `(?![\w-])` trailing guard is inconsistent with the leading boundary handled only by `\b` (a date preceded by a letter like 'x2024-01-01' would be caught by `\b` boundary anyway), and the day never allows 3-day months distinction, which matches the stated task assumptions. Overall robust and minimal.
